# ECN-2026-029 - Change notice - Machining induction billet heater #1

Revision: Rev D  
Plant: P1, line P1-L3  
Equipment: EQ-P1-L3-IH01

Reason for change
- Background: During routine review of process capability and furnace performance logs, machining downstream feedback indicated variability in billet hardening and surface finish attributed to inconsistent feed temperature at the machining cell. Analysis of heater control logs and metallurgical reports identified that the setpoint for the induction billet heater did not match the metallurgical profile used for forging and machining acceptance. To align the thermal input with metallurgical specification and reduce rework, the heater setpoint is being standardized.
- Objective: Establish a verified target billet temperature for EQ-P1-L3-IH01 to reduce process variability, improve dimensional stability at machining, and reduce downstream scrap and rework events.
- Change statement: The target billet temperature for Machining induction billet heater #1 (EQ-P1-L3-IH01) is 1235 °C. This replaces the previous undocumented practice of operator-adjusted setpoints and moves the setting into controlled documentation and automated control limits.

Affected items
- Equipment: EQ-P1-L3-IH01 (Machining induction billet heater #1) control setpoint and associated control logic parameters.
- Process: Billet feed into P1-L3 machining cell, heat soak and transfer procedures upstream of machining operations.
- Procedures and records: SOP-P1-L3-01, SOP-P1-L3-02 require revision to capture the new target temperature, verification steps, and acceptance criteria. Training records and calibration logs associated with EQ-P1-L3-IH01 must be updated.
- Materials: Billets processed for the P1-L3 line while EQ-P1-L3-IH01 is operating under the new setpoint; traceability records must reference the setpoint change for affected production lots.

Implementation
- Control change: Update the control system setpoint for EQ-P1-L3-IH01 to the specified target. Configure the heater control profile such that the billet temperature at transfer is validated against the target. Logging must capture setpoint, measured billet temperature, and operator acknowledgement on each charge.
- Procedure updates: Revise SOP-P1-L3-01 and SOP-P1-L3-02 to include:
  - The target billet temperature for EQ-P1-L3-IH01 is 1235 °C as the required setpoint for billets entering the machining cell.
  - Pre-transfer verification method and acceptable variance description (refer to metallurgical acceptance criteria in related documentation).
  - Operator steps for initiating the controlled setpoint, monitoring temperature, and recording the measured value in the production log.
  - Escalation and hold procedures when measured temperature does not meet the documented acceptance criteria.
- Verification and validation: Prior to full production use, perform a controlled validation run with documented measurements demonstrating stable approach to the target temperature and consistent transfer temperature at the machining interface. Document metallurgical test results and machining sample inspections to demonstrate reduced variability.
- Training: Conduct targeted training for operations and maintenance personnel covering:
  - Rationale for the setpoint change and expected impact on machining quality.
  - How to engage the updated control logic for EQ-P1-L3-IH01.
  - Required logging and deviation reporting steps per the updated SOPs.
  - Maintenance response for control alarms related to temperature deviation.
- Maintenance and calibration: Ensure temperature sensors and control loops associated with EQ-P1-L3-IH01 are within calibration and that any drift is corrected before adoption. Record sensor calibration status in equipment maintenance records.
- Records to keep:
  - Control system change log documenting the setpoint change entry for EQ-P1-L3-IH01 and approval traceability.
  - Validation run report including measured billet temperatures, process conditions, and machining inspection results.
  - Revised SOP-P1-L3-01 and SOP-P1-L3-02 versions showing incorporation of the target temperature and new verification steps.
  - Training sign-off sheets for all affected operators and maintenance staff.
  - Production logs showing ongoing compliance with the target billet temperature for each shift or charge as required by the revised SOPs.
  - Any deviation reports and corrective action records if billets are processed outside the acceptance window.
- Examples:
  - Example entry in the production log must show the equipment id, the setpoint reference, measured billet temperature at transfer, and operator initials as required by the revised SOPs.
  - Example validation documentation should include metallurgical sample id, measured hardness or microstructure notes, and reference to the production lot processed under the new setpoint.

Approvals
- Engineering: Approval required for configuration changes to the heater control logic and for acceptance of validation test results.
- Operations: Approval required to update SOP-P1-L3-01 and SOP-P1-L3-02 and to commence production under the new target.
- Quality: Approval required for metallurgical acceptance criteria and sign-off on validation demonstrating reduced variability at machining.
- Maintenance: Approval required to confirm calibration and readiness of sensors and actuators before change implementation.

Related documents
- ECN-2026-022
- SOP-P1-L3-01
- SOP-P1-L3-02

Change authority and sign-off dates must be recorded in the document control system with references to the above related documents. All implementation actions shall be tracked against the approvals listed and retained in the permanent engineering change record for audit and continuous improvement purposes.
